q: 1. The earnest money deposited by unsuccessful bidder is returned after ............
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) acts as a guarantee that the bidder will enter the contract. Once the contract is officially awarded to the winner, the money is returned to the unsuccessful parties.

q: 2. Which of the following is the ultimate method of dispute resolution in any contract ............
explain: While arbitration and DRBs are common, 'Litigation' in a court of law is the final legal recourse if all alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods fail.

q: 3. The bid review committee consists of ............ members of persons.
explain: In many public procurement frameworks, a three-member committee is standardized to ensure fairness and collective decision-making during bid evaluation.

q: 4. The penalty provision in any contract agreement is ............
explain: Liquidated damages or penalties for delay are commonly set at 0.05% of the contract price per day, often capped at 10% of the total value.

q: 5. The minimum number of consulting firms for direct purchase of service is ............
explain: In competitive procurement environments, usually at least 3 firms are required to ensure a fair price comparison for service acquisition.

q: 6. The department head can extend the time upto ............% of initial contract duration.
explain: Administrative rules often limit the authority of a department head to approve time extensions to 25% of the original duration; beyond this, higher approval is usually required.

q: 7. The pre-tender stage of construction requires ............
explain: Before a tender is invited, the owner must ensure the land is available, the site is chosen, and the technical scope (design) is finalized.

q: 8. The post tender stage of construction consists of ............
explain: The post-tender phase covers everything from contract award through execution monitoring to the final settlement of accounts.

q: 9. Direct cost a project is due to ............
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Direct costs are expenses directly attributable to a specific work item, such as labor wages and material costs.

q: 10. Total project cost ............
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Note: This question in the text appears to repeat the concept of direct cost. The answer 'd' refers to the core direct components.

q: 11. Total cost is ............
explain: The total project cost is the summation of Direct Costs and Indirect Costs (including overheads and contingency).

q: 12. The maximum amount of advance payment (mobilization fund) permitted is ............ of contract amount.
explain: According to standard public procurement rules, the mobilization advance is generally capped at 20% of the contract price to help the contractor start the work.

q: 13. The first stage of construction is ............
explain: Every construction project begins with the 'initiation of proposal' where the need for the project is identified and feasibility is assessed.

q: 14. The best method of procurement for complex and work of specific nature is ............
explain: International Competitive Bidding (ICB) is preferred for complex projects to ensure a wide range of expert bidders and competitive global pricing.

q: 15. During the construction period, price variation clause in contracts caters to ............
options: increase in rates of only important materials
variation in cost in materials element, labour element and petrol-oil-lubricant element
variation in total cost of the project on an ad hoc basis
explain: A comprehensive price variation clause accounts for fluctuations in the core cost components: labor, materials, and fuel (POL).

q: 16. Mobilization advance up to 10% of the cost of work is given to a contractor ............
options: on commencement of work at site for payment of loan taken by him
for the purchase of construction materials
for the payment of advances to labour and other staff
for all activities required to start the work at site on finalization of the contract document
explain: Mobilization advance is specifically provided to help the contractor with initial expenses like setting up site offices, moving machinery, and procuring initial supplies.

q: 17. Security deposit deducted at 5% from contractor's bills is ............
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period of six months or one monsoon whichever is later is over
explain: The security deposit (retention money) is held to ensure the contractor fixes any defects that appear during the Defect Liability Period (DLP).

q: 18. The main criteria for selection of contractors to execute work is ............
explain: Pre-qualification and selection involve evaluating a contractor's financial stability, technical expertise, available equipment, and past project experience.

q: 19. Best option to avoid the undue pressure, cartels and collusion during bidding process is ............
explain: Electronic bidding (E-bidding) increases transparency and prevents physical cartels or collusion between bidders because the process is digitized and hidden until the deadline.

q: 20. Which is not the part of bidding documents ............
explain: While the Invitation for Bid (IFB) advertises the project, the 'Bidding Documents' usually refer to the technical and legal package (drawings, specs, contract) provided to the bidder.

q: 21. A written offer submitted by contractors to execute certain work at certain rates within the fixed time is called .............
explain: A tender (or bid) is the formal offer submitted by a contractor in response to an invitation to carry out work at a specified price.

q: 22. Which of the following is a primary process for procurement of goods and services from a competitive market?
explain: Bidding is the standard competitive process used by organizations to select vendors or contractors based on price and capability.

q: 23. Public procurement monitoring office (P.P.M.O.) can blacklist the bidders disobeying the code of conduct upto ............. years.
explain: According to typical public procurement regulations (like those in Nepal), blacklisting can range from 1 to 3 years depending on the severity.

q: 24. The employer shall pay the interim bill within ............. days after the bill submitted by the contractor.
explain: 30 days is the standard industry timeframe for processing and paying interim progress certificates.

q: 25. Maximum amount that can be paid to the contractor as a prize for the early finishing of the works is equal to .............% of the contract amount.
explain: In many procurement systems, bonus payments for early completion are capped at 10% of the total contract value.

q: 26. Percentage of retention money is equal to .............% of each payment made to the contractor.
explain: Retention money is usually deducted at 5% from each interim bill to act as a safeguard against defects.

q: 27. Which of the following is not a bid document?
explain: A Letter of Acceptance is issued *after* the bidding process is finished to signify the award of the contract; it is not part of the initial bid package.

q: 28. The purpose of bid evaluation is to evaluate .............
explain: Evaluation aims to find the bidder who meets all technical requirements (substantially responsive) at the best price.

q: 29. As per public the public procurement regulation 2064, who approves the prequalification criteria?
explain: In the Nepalese PPR 2064 framework, the Head of the Department (Department Chief) holds the authority to approve these criteria.

q: 30. In a sealed quotation, the successful bidder should deliver the performance security within ............. days of receipt of letter of acceptance.
explain: For sealed quotations (usually smaller works), a shorter period like 7 days is standard for providing security.

q: 31. The remuneration of dispute adjudication board is paid by .............
explain: To ensure impartiality, the costs of a DAB are typically shared equally (50/50) between the Employer (Client) and the Contractor.

q: 32. The money deposited by the contractor as the guarantee of tender is known as .............
explain: Bid bond and earnest money are both terms for the security deposit required when submitting a tender.

q: 33. Which of the following is done first in procurement of consulting services .............
explain: Expression of Interest (EOI) is the first step to identify capable firms before shortlisting and requesting a formal proposal (RFP).

q: 34. The maximum amount of project cost after the price adjustment should not exceed .............
explain: Many local regulations cap the total price adjustment (escalation) at 15% of the original contract price.

q: 35. E.O.I. is compulsory for procurement of consulting services if work amount exceeds .............
explain: As per PPR 2064, public notification for EOI is mandatory for consulting services above 2 million (20 Lakhs).

q: 36. While procuring the consulting services, R.F.P. is extended to ..............
explain: In the procurement of consulting services, an Expression of Interest (EOI) is conducted first. The Request for Proposal (RFP) is then specifically issued only to those firms that have been shortlisted.

q: 37. If a contractor is found corrupt for tender work, then what should be done by concerned office?
explain: Under standard procurement rules, if corruption is detected during the tender process, the immediate administrative action is the cancellation of that contractor's tender.

q: 38. The authority of variation order up to 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: In accordance with Nepalese Public Procurement regulations, the Department Head (Chief) generally has the delegated authority to approve variations up to a certain percentage (25%).

q: 39. The authority of variation order above 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: Major variations exceeding standard departmental limits (typically above 25%) require higher-level approval from the Council of Ministers (Cabinet).

q: 40. While bid evaluation, if unit rate and total amount are contradicted, then which of the following will prevail ..............
options: unit price is adopted and total amount is corrected
explain: Standard procurement guidelines (including PPMO) state that the unit price quoted in words or figures prevails. If the total is wrong due to a calculation error, the unit rate is used to correct the total.

q: 41. In Q.C.B.S. method of procurement, evaluation of consulting firms to award the contract, the weightage will be ..............
explain: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) typically gives high priority to technical competence. A common standard weightage is 80% for the technical proposal and 20% for the financial proposal.

q: 42. Bid bond is ............% of quoted amount.
explain: Commonly, Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or Bid Bonds range from 1% to 2.5% of the estimated cost.

q: 43. Direct purchase can be done for procurement of consulting services or construction works upto ............
options: 5 lakh in case of consulting services
5 lakh in case of construction works
explain: Specific financial thresholds for direct purchase vary by regional governing rules, but 5 lakh is generally not the standard limit for both simultaneously.

q: 44. In the L.I.B. type of contract management, the acronym stands for ..............
explain: Wait, correcting from earlier: In the context of international procurement, LIB often refers to Limited International Bidding, which is used when there are only a limited number of suppliers.

q: 45. The pre qualification criteria is approved by ..............
explain: In standard government procurement in Nepal, major tender criteria (like pre-qualification) are officially approved by the Department Head (Director General).

q: 46. For the I.C.B. procurement method, the period of bidding to contractor must be at least ..............
explain: For International Competitive Bidding (ICB), standard regulations require a minimum bidding period of 45 days to allow international firms sufficient time to prepare proposals.

q: 47. The opening of bidding in the process of procurement is
explain: Tendering is the process by which an organization invites bids for large projects. It includes the invitation, submission, and opening of bids.

q: 48. Consulting works worth more than 10 crores NRs should be procured on the basis of
explain: According to Nepalese procurement regulations, high-value consulting services (above 100 million NPR) require an Expression of Interest (EOI) followed by a Request for Proposal (RFP) at an international level.

q: 49. The estimated cost of works must be quoted in the tender notice for works worth up to
explain: Standard procurement practice in Nepal typically requires the estimated cost to be disclosed in the notice for works valued up to 20 million (2 Crore) NPR to guide bidders.

q: 50. The price adjustment clause is essential for contract having duration greater than _______ months.
explain: Under the Public Procurement Act of Nepal, a price adjustment clause is generally mandatory for contracts with a duration exceeding 12 months to account for inflation.
